title: Grateful Dead Live at Kongressaal - Deutsches Museum on 1972-05-18
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v7.02 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) D

ai_review.summary: Stunning Charlie Miller soundboard capture of a high‑energy 5/18/72 show featuring a smoking Dark Star > Morning Dew, stellar Good Lovin', and an all‑time great It Hurts Me Too.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crystal‑clear soundboard mix praised for its superb balance and minimal tape hiss, letting the band’s tight, jazzy playing shine through. Musically the concert is a highlight of the Europe ’72 tour – the first set bursts out with Truckin' and Good Lovin', while the second set delivers a monumental Dark Star > Morning Dew, a blistering It Hurts Me Too, and a knockout Casey Jones. Overall the performance feels both relaxed and intensely focused, making it one of the era’s most celebrated shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive 4‑5 star reviews (10 out of 11) praise both the musical performance and the soundboard recording; the few minor criticisms are outweighed by repeated acclaim for standout songs and excellent mix.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix with only faint tape hiss in quiet passages; praised for superb mastering by Charlie Miller, no significant drop‑outs or distortion reported.

poor_songs: Sing Me Back Home (considered a slog by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set launches with high‑energy Truckin' and tight jams, maintaining momentum into a dynamic second set anchored by the epic Dark Star>Morning Dew segue; the encore rounds out the night on a soaring note.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead guitar tone described as 'stupendous' and his vocal performance on Morning Dew noted as emotive and powerful; jazzy leads praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass work highlighted as a ‘bomb’ with notable solos, especially during the Dark Star and It Hurts Me Too sections; tight interplay with keyboards emphasized.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar and vocal duet with Garcia receive praise for adding depth to jams; solid rhythmic foundation noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Dual‑keyboard texture lauded – Keith's piano blends beautifully with Pigpen's organ, especially on Morning Dew; overall keyboard work called 'gorgeous' and essential to the show’s dynamics.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy's drumming praised for tasteful breaks (e.g., after Morning Dew) and maintaining a powerful groove; no major issues reported.
